translation_en: Ubai­dullah ibn Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: My paternal uncle narrated to me; my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah sent for the Ansar, gathered them in a pavilion, and said, “Be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger, for I will be at the Hawd.”

Thabit ibn Muhammad narrated to me: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet prayed at night, he would say, “O Allah, our Lord, praise belongs to You. You sustain the heavens and earth, and You are Lord and Light of the heavens and earth and all in them. You are the Truth; Your word, promise, meeting You, Paradise, the Fire, and the Hour are true. O Allah, to You I submit, in You I believe, upon You I rely, to You I turn in dispute, and by You I judge. Forgive what I sent ahead and left behind, concealed and declared, and what You know better than I. There is no god but You.” Abu Abdullah said: Qays ibn Sa‘d and Abu al-Zubayr reported from Tawus “Qayyam.” Mujahid said “Al-Qayyum” means the One standing over everything. Umar recited “Al-Qayyam”; both are praise.

Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Al-A‘mash narrated to me, from Khaythamah, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “There is none of you except that his Lord will speak to him, with no interpreter between them and no veil screening Him.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, from Abu Imran, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, from his father, from the Prophet, who said, “Two gardens will have vessels of silver and everything in them of silver, and two gardens will have vessels of gold and everything in them of gold. Between the people and seeing their Lord there will be nothing but the cloak of grandeur upon His Face in the Garden of Eden.”

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Abd al-Malik ibn A‘yan and Jami ibn Abi Rashid narrated to us, from Abu Wa’il, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “Whoever takes a Muslim’s property by a false oath will meet Allah while He is angry with him.” Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah then recited as confirmation from the Book of Allah: “Those who purchase a small gain at the cost of Allah’s covenant and their oaths will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them…” Quran 3:77.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said, “There are three whom Allah will not speak to or look at on the Day of Resurrection: a man who falsely swears about a commodity that he was offered more for it than he was; a man who swears a false oath after Asr to take a Muslim’s property; and a man who withholds surplus water. Allah will say, ‘Today I will withhold My bounty from you, just as you withheld the surplus of what your hands did not make.’”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Bakrah, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet, who said, “Time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and earth. The year has twelve months, four sacred: three in succession, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha‘ban.” He asked, “What month is this?” We said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He remained silent until we thought he would name it differently, then said, “Is it not Dhu al-Hijjah?” We said yes. He asked, “What land is this?” We said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He remained silent until we thought he would name it differently, then said, “Is it not the Sacred Land?” We said yes. He asked, “What day is this?” We said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He remained silent until we thought he would name it differently, then said, “Is it not the Day of Sacrifice?” We said yes. He said, “Your blood and property”—Muhammad said, “I think he also said your honor”—“are sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day, in this land, in this month. You will meet your Lord and He will ask you about your deeds. Do not return after me to misguidance, striking one another’s necks. Let those present convey this to the absent; perhaps some who receive it will understand it better than some who heard it.” Whenever Muhammad mentioned it, he said, “The Prophet spoke the truth,” then, “Have I conveyed it? Have I conveyed it?”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us: Abd al-Wahid narrated to us: Asim narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Usamah, who said: A son of one of the Prophet’s daughters was dying, so she sent for him. He sent word, “To Allah belongs what He takes and gives, and everything has an appointed term. Be patient and seek reward.” She sent for him again and adjured him to come. The Messenger of Allah rose, and I rose with him, along with Muadh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, and Ubadah ibn al-Samit. When we entered, they handed the child to him while his breath rattled in his chest—I think he said it was like an old waterskin. The Messenger of Allah wept. Sa‘d ibn Ubadah said, “Are you weeping?” He replied, “Allah shows mercy only to those of His servants who are merciful.”

Ubai­dullah ibn Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Ya‘qub narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said, “Paradise and the Fire disputed before their Lord. Paradise said, ‘My Lord, why do only the weak and lowly among people enter me?’ The Fire said, ‘I have been favored with the arrogant.’ Allah said to Paradise, ‘You are My mercy,’ and to the Fire, ‘You are My punishment; through you I punish whom I will. Each of you will be filled.’ Allah does not wrong any of His creation. He will create for the Fire whom He wills, and they will be cast into it. It will say, ‘Is there any more?’ three times, until He places His Foot in it; then it will be filled, its parts will draw together, and it will say, ‘Enough, enough, enough.’”

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, who said, “Some people will be touched by the scorching of the Fire as punishment for sins they committed. Then Allah will admit them to Paradise by His mercy, and they will be called the Jahannamiyyun.” Hammam said: Qatadah narrated to us: Anas narrated to us, from the Prophet.

Musa narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: A Jewish scholar came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “O Muhammad, Allah will place the heaven on one finger, the earth on one finger, the mountains on one finger, the trees and rivers on one finger, and all the rest of creation on one finger. Then He will say with His hand, ‘I am the King.’” The Messenger of Allah laughed and said, “They have not appraised Allah with the appraisal due to Him” Quran 6:91.

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far informed us: Sharik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir informed me, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I spent a night in Maymunah’s house while the Prophet was there, to see how he prayed at night. He spoke with his family for a while, then slept. During the last third of the night, or some of it, he sat up, looked at the sky, and recited, “Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and earth…” through “for people of understanding” Quran 2:164. Then he got up, performed ablution, and used a tooth-stick. He prayed eleven rak‘ahs. Bilal called the prayer, and he prayed two units, then went out and led the dawn prayer.

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “When Allah had finished creating creation, He wrote with Him above His Throne: ‘My mercy preceded My anger.’”

Adam narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Al-A‘mash narrated to us: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb say: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud say: The Messenger of Allah, the truthful one who was believed, narrated to us: “Each of you is formed in his mother’s womb for forty days and forty nights, then is a clinging clot for the same, then a lump of flesh for the same. Then the angel is sent and commanded to write four things: his provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed. Then the soul is breathed into him. A man may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise until only an arm’s length remains between him and it, but what was written overtakes him, so he acts with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. A man may act with the deeds of the people of the Fire until only an arm’s length remains between him and it, but what was written overtakes him, so he acts with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.”

Khallad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Umar ibn Dharr narrated to us: I heard my father narrate, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet said, “O Gabriel, what prevents you from visiting us more often?” Then this was revealed: “We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us…” to the end of the verse Quran 19:64. He said: This was the answer to Muhammad.

Yahya narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah in a cultivated area in Medina while he leaned on a palm stalk. He passed a group of Jews, and some said, “Ask him about the Spirit.” Others said, “Do not ask him.” They asked him, so he stood leaning on the stalk, and I was behind him. I thought revelation was coming to him, and he said, “They ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given only a little knowledge” Quran 17:85. Some of them said to one another, “We told you not to ask him.”

Ismail narrated to me: Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “Allah has undertaken the care of the one who strives in His cause; nothing takes him out except striving in His cause and belief in His words: either He admits him to Paradise or returns him to the home from which he departed with the reward or booty he gained.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Abu Musa, who said: A man came to the Prophet and said, “A man fights out of zeal, another bravely, and another to be seen. Which is in Allah’s cause?” He said, “Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme is in Allah’s cause.”

Shihab ibn Abbad narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ismail, from Qays, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said: I heard the Prophet say, “There will always be a group from my community prevailing over the people until Allah’s command comes to them.”

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Ibn Jabir narrated to us: Umayr ibn Hani narrated to me that he heard Muawiyah say: I heard the Prophet say, “There will always be a community from my people standing by Allah’s command. Those who deny them and those who oppose them will not harm them, until Allah’s command comes while they remain so.” Malik ibn Yakhamir said, “I heard Muadh say, ‘They are in Syria.’” Muawiyah said, “This is Malik claiming that he heard Muadh say that they are in Syria.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Husayn: Nafi ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet stood before Musaylimah among his companions and said, “If you asked me for this piece, I would not give it to you. You will not go beyond what Allah has decreed for you; and if you turn away, Allah will surely strike you down.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us, from Abd al-Wahid, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas‘ud, who said: As I walked with the Prophet in one of Medina’s cultivated areas while he leaned on a palm stalk he carried, we passed some Jews. Some said, “Ask him about the Spirit.” Others said, “Do not ask him, lest he tell you something you dislike.” Some said, “We will ask him.” One stood and said, “O Abu al-Qasim, what is the Spirit?” The Prophet was silent, and I knew revelation was coming. He said, “They ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given only a little knowledge” Quran 17:85. Al-A‘mash said: This is how it is in our recitation.

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “Allah has guaranteed the one who strives in His cause—nothing took him out except striving in His cause and belief in His words—that He will admit him to Paradise or return him to his home with the reward or booty he gained.”

Musaddad narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “When you supplicate to Allah, be resolute in your supplication. None of you should say, ‘If You will, give this to me,’ for no one can compel Allah.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ismail narrated to us: My brother Abd al-Hamid narrated to me, from Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq, from Ibn Shihab, from Ali ibn Husayn, that Husayn ibn Ali informed him, that Ali ibn Abi Talib informed him: The Messenger of Allah came to him and Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah, one night and said, “Will you not pray?” Ali said: I replied, “O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in Allah’s hand; when He wills to raise us, He raises us.” The Messenger of Allah turned away and said nothing. Then I heard him as he walked away, striking his thigh and saying, “Man is the most argumentative of things” Quran 18:54.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us: Fulayh narrated to us: Hilal ibn Ali narrated to us, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “The believer is like a tender crop: the wind bends its leaves whichever way it comes, and when it subsides it straightens. The believer is likewise bent by affliction. The disbeliever is like a firm cedar, standing upright until Allah breaks it whenever He wills.”

Al-Hakam ibn Nafi informed us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Salim ibn Abdullah informed me that Abdullah ibn Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, standing on the pulpit, say, “Your remaining time, compared with the nations before you, is like the time between Asr prayer and sunset. The people of the Torah were given the Torah and acted by it until midday, then became unable, and were given one qirat each. The people of the Gospel were given the Gospel and acted by it until Asr, then became unable, and were given one qirat each. You were given the Quran and acted by it until sunset, and were given two qirats each.” The people of the Torah said, “Our Lord, these people did less work but received more reward.” He said, “Have I withheld any of your reward?” They said, “No.” He said, “That is My favor; I give it to whom I will.”

Abdullah al-Musnadi narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah among a group of men. He said, “I take your pledge that you will not associate anything with Allah, steal, commit adultery, kill your children, bring a false accusation you fabricate between your hands and feet, or disobey me in what is right. Whoever fulfills this, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of these and is punished for it in this world, that is an expiation and purification for him. Whoever Allah conceals, the matter is up to Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.”

Mu‘alla ibn Asad narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, that Solomon, the Prophet of Allah, had sixty wives. He said, “Tonight I will go around to my wives; let each conceive and give birth to a horseman who will fight in Allah’s cause.” He went around to them, but none gave birth except one, who bore half a boy. The Prophet of Allah said, “If Solomon had made the exception, every one of them would have conceived and given birth to a horseman who would fight in Allah’s cause.”

Muhammad narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us: Khalid al-Hadhdha narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah visited a Bedouin who was ill. He said, “There is no harm for you; it is a purification, if Allah wills.” The Bedouin said, “A purification? No, it is a fever boiling over an old man and taking him to the graves.” The Prophet said, “Then so be it.”
